rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should explore a representative multimodal configuration. This test uses scgpt (advanced RNA encoder) and imagenet_vit_l (strong image encoder) with concat fusion, which balances simplicity and potential performance. It clarifies the baseline effectiveness of these components, reducing uncertainty about encoder choices and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (singleprofile, concat fusion) achieved 0.4348 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (more data) with weighted fusion (vs concat) and avgpool aggregation, which could improve performance by leveraging more complex interactions. It balances exploration (profile setting) and exploitation (using scgpt RNA/imagenet_vit_l image encoders from config_001).

Existing evidence shows config_020 (validation accuracy 0.542) is the best so far. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method identical. This clarifies if transformer aggregation improves upon the current best, balancing exploitation of config_020's success with exploration of aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation and resnet50 image encoder (config_029) could further improve performance, while maintaining scgpt RNA encoder and weighted fusion. It directly builds on the promising multiprofile/scgpt foundation, exploring critical design choices (aggregation/image encoder) with minimal deviation from the current top performer.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests transformer aggregation and concat fusion with the same RNA/image encoders, clarifying whether aggregation/fusion choices are critical. It balances exploitation (using proven encoders) with exploration of aggregation methods, which are key design choices with sparse evidence.

Existing evidence shows config_020 (avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests changing the fusion method to concat while keeping the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation, clarifying if fusion type significantly impacts performance. It's the best next step as it builds on the current best configuration, exploring a key design choice with minimal parameter change.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (0.542 accuracy) is the top performer using scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other parameters the same, to determine if this change could improve accuracy. It directly addresses uncertainty about the optimal image encoder for this setup, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of alternative components.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (0.542 accuracy) is the top performer with scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, exploring if changing the RNA encoder or aggregation method could improve performance. It balances exploitation (using weighted fusion from config_020) with exploration of RNA encoder and aggregation variations, which are key design choices with uncertain optimal settings.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests config_047 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion), which varies the image encoder. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice (ViT vs ResNet) impacts performance, potentially uncovering a better configuration. Since only one experiment remains, testing a closely related high-potential variant of the top-performing config is the best use of the budget.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while retaining resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion could yield higher accuracy. It leverages the proven effectiveness of transformer and weighted fusion while exploring a different RNA encoder, balancing exploration and exploitation under the final budget constraint.
